stories.headline: Pistons kick off season vs. Celtics with NBA's largest opening day comeback
stories.summary: The Pistons rallied from a 22-point deficit against the Celtics to pull off the largest comeback on the first day of an NBA season in the play-by-play era.
stories.body:
DETROIT -- Midway through the third quarter Tuesday, the Detroit Pistons fell behind 72-50 to the Boston Celtics in front of their home crowd after a 3-pointer from Paul George. It was at that moment the intensity level flipped for the Pistons, who went on to pull off the largest comeback on the first day of an NBA season in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98).

The 22-point rally also marked Detroit's largest come-from-behind win against Boston over the past 30 seasons.

"The opponent doesn't matter. What people say doesn't matter," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. "The only thing that matters is if we play Pistons basketball. I thought tonight we found enough stretches where we did, and when we played Pistons basketball, we're hard to beat. That's the only thing that matters."

Detroit would use a 23-0 run in the fourth quarter to pull ahead and beat the Celtics 121-113 during a rare Tuesday afternoon tip-off.

The Pistons trailed 99-89 with 8:19 left, then led 112-99 with 3:33 remaining. That run tied their largest in a game over the past 10 seasons, according to ESPN Research.

Veteran sharpshooter Duncan Robinson went off in the fourth quarter, contributing 15 of his 21 points while knocking down three 3-pointers. All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham, who did not speak to reporters after the game, also contributed 8 of his 22 points in the fourth and finished with eight assists.

All-NBA center Jalen Duren, fresh off signing a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract, recorded 22 points and nine rebounds in a strong performance.

Duren said the Pistons' comeback "just embodied the culture and what we're trying to build here."

"We're a team that's known to be gritty, known to get it out the mud, known to never quit, and that's our identity," Duren said. "Even the guys who are new here are embodying that. And that's why we were able to have the outcome that we had."

The Pistons trailed 58-45 at halftime after falling behind by as many as 15 in the opening half.

George, making his Celtics debut, exploded for a game-high 38 points, while Jayson Tatum added 13 points and 11 assists on 6-for-23 shooting. Pistons forward Ausar Thompson took on the challenge of guarding Tatum.

"Coach gives me the toughest matchup every night. I don't want them to score," said Thompson, who had 11 points and five assists. "I just try to do what I can to help the team win on that end and it's a tough matchup."

As part of the opening day festivities, the Pistons hosted a special blue carpet arrival outside of Little Caesars Arena. Duren participated and said he wasn't nervous to face the fans after a four-month contract standoff that spanned over the summer and start of training camp.

"I wasn't nervous. I know the true fans know how much I love them and know how much I care about this city," Duren said. "Obviously, business is business, but I was excited to be back in this jersey and put on for the fans."

Cunningham also delivered a pregame message to set the stage. He grabbed the microphone at center court after introductions and shared the Pistons' "big plans this year" as they look to do something "special in this city."

"All my teammates, the entire Pistons organization wants to say thank you for all the love and support," Cunningham told the fans. "This team, we come from all over the place but we're grateful to be able to call Detroit home now."

Cunningham says they've been putting in the work all offseason and believe in each other as a group coming off a 60-win season.

"The NBA wanted to start the league off in Detroit this season. Let's start it off right. Let's get to work," Cunningham said.

stories.headline: NFL chief medical officer: Eagles' approach to Hurts was 'appropriately guarded'
stories.summary: At the owners meetings Tuesday in New York, NFL officials staunchly defended the process involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot issue, with chief medical officer Allen Sills addressing reporters in a media availability.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- NFL officials Tuesday staunchly defended the medical process involving Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clot issue.

NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills was blunt in a news conference from the owners meetings.

"The notion that there's external factors that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way -- that's nonsense," Sills said.

The NFL is not punishing the Eagles for the handling of Hurts, who was cleared to play before Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after he was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf.

Hurts, 28, is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs days after the game. Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for around three months.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs.

NFL officials confirmed Tuesday that it had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and Cleveland Clinic London throughout the process of Hurts being treated. Sills called the Eagles' treatment of Hurts "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step."

This week's news prompted rampant speculation about why the Eagles allowed Hurts to play in London.

Jeff Miller, NFL executive vice president overseeing player health and safety, called such speculation "considerable and uninformed," as well as "unfounded."

"Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts' health was always made the first priority and continues to be," Miller said.

The NFL declined to discuss specifics of Hurts' case, citing medical privacy. But Sills, who has been a team physical for three decades, said he has "tremendous confidence" in the Eagles' medical staff. The NFL works one to two years in advance of international games to prep for medical care, identifying local hospitals, physicians and resources at every site.

The medical experts tasked with evaluating players in such cases are not influenced by the team, Sills said.

"There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person. Period," Sills said.

Doctors speculating online about "what should have been done" without all the data or being in the room with a patient are "unprofessional and unethical" in doing so, Sills said, citing a "sacred trust" between physicians and patients.

The NFL has tracked blood clot cases every season for the last decade and shares the data with the NFLPA, Sills said. Each year features a handful of cases.

"This isn't really a new situation, but it's something we examine," Sills said.

The threshold for people flying with superficial blood clots, which Hurts did on the way home from London, depends on the "nuances of each situation," Sills said, adding that the NFL spends significant time planning for player safety as it relates to long flights for international play.

stories.headline: Football watchdog chair asserts 'absolute' power to force City sale
stories.summary: The Independent Football Regulator will have "absolute power" to force Manchester City's owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog's chair has said.
stories.body:
The Independent Football Regulator will have "absolute power" to force Manchester City's owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog's chair has said.

City have been found guilty of circumventing Premier League rules by an independent commission, which found they set up "sham" commercial arrangements to inflate revenues or reduce costs by over £900 million ($1.2 billion) over a nine-season period.

They were also found to have made "concerted efforts" to "stop and frustrate" the Premier League's investigation into those arrangements.

David Kogan, the chair of the IFR, told "The Rest Is Football" podcast it was premature to talk about any action his organisation might take, with City having lodged an appeal against the original commission's verdict.

However, he confirmed the IFR had the power to force a sale by the club's owner Sheikh Mansour if that was felt to be appropriate.

"We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety," Kogan said.

Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan replied: "No, no, no. We've got absolute power to do so."

On the possibility of the IFR investigating City, Kogan said: "I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we've seen all of those questions being answered and then we will have to decide whether we're going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we're going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake."

Kogan has already pledged to resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City, amid concerns it could become a diplomatic issue between the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.headline: Sources: Barcelona report PSG to UEFA for 'aggressive' tifo
stories.summary: Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the tifo unfurled by the French club's supporters before Tuesday's Champions League game, a source told ESPN.
stories.body:
Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the tifo unfurled by the French club's supporters before Tuesday's Champions League game, a source told ESPN.

As the players came on to the pitch before kickoff, fans behind one of the goals at Parc des Princes held up a giant banner which showed a masked figure carrying a chainsaw and destroying the Barça badge.

Underneath were the words: "Massacre, Parisian style."

In addition, pyrotechnics were used to mimic the sparks coming from the chainsaw as it hacked away at the Barça crest.

The source said the imagery evoked was both "overly aggressive and offensive."

On the pitch, PSG ran out 4-2 winners in an entertaining game between two of Europe's most in-form sides.

Desiré Douré, Lucas Hernández, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz were all on target as PSG made it three wins out of three in the Champions League this season.

For Barça, who twice levelled through Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal, it represented their first loss of the season, bringing an end to their 11-game winning streak.

Both teams have big games to come in their respective leagues this weekend.

PSG face Lyon in a top-of-the-table clash in Ligue 1, while Barça host rivals Real Madrid in the Clásico.

stories.headline: Brewers fans cashing in 2015 promo irked by World Series seats
stories.summary: The Brewers are trying to make amends for not living up "to the spirit of the program" stemming from a 2015 "Timeless Ticket" promotion if they paid $1,000.
stories.body:
MILWAUKEE -- The Milwaukee Brewers ran a promotion over a decade ago offering fans a "Timeless Ticket" granting them admission to any game in the future if they paid $1,000.

Now that the Brewers are in the World Series for the first time since 1982, fans who took that deal are eager to redeem those tickets they bought in 2015. That has led to some complications.

Brewers president of business operations Rick Schlesinger said Tuesday that several hundred fans had indicated they wanted to redeem their Timeless Tickets for a World Series game. Schlesinger acknowledged that "we subsequently erred in our internal communications on the logistics of fulfilling the requests."

"While we were able to accommodate all with seats, we received feedback from some that they were unhappy with their seat locations," Schlesinger said. "Clearly, even with extraordinary limitations on available seats, we did not live up to the spirit of the program, and we have been working through a resolution."

Danny Fochesato of Milwaukee bought a Timeless Ticket on his 27th birthday, planning all along to redeem it whenever the Brewers reached the World Series.

The promotion enabled a Timeless Ticket holder to redeem that ticket and become eligible to buy three additional tickets to that game for the full retail price. The offer said the tickets "may be redeemed for the best available seat locations, subject to ticket availability at the time of redemption."

"Back in 2015, that was a big selling point from the sales people about this," Fochesato said. "They really touted, 'Hey, this is going to be the best available seats. You're getting the priority just behind season-ticket holders. Anything the season-ticket holders don't have, you'll have dibs at it for the World Series.' That's kind of the story they sold."

That would have worked out fine when Fochesato tried redeeming his Timeless Ticket for a potential World Series game in 2018, when the Brewers reached the National League Championship Series.

Fochesato said he got four tickets in the 100 level behind home plate that he could have used if the Brewers had made the World Series that year, when they ended up losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 7 of the NLCS.

This time, he wasn't as fortunate.

"We had a form, and it only had 400-level or standing-room options," Fochesato said. "We couldn't even know what game we had. We just had to put a preference of which ones we wanted, and then we had to submit the form and just sit and wait for them what we got. I immediately was like, 'No, that's bogus.'"

Fochesato said he bargained his way to three 400-level seats for Saturday's Game 2 with the Tampa Bay Rays and one lower-level seat in the right-field corner for Friday's Game 1.

He said he was in line for the public sale of tickets and saw better seats were available than those that were offered to him under the Timeless Ticket program.

The Brewers are trying to make amends.

Schlesinger said any Timeless Ticket holder who applied for World Series tickets before the deadline will now get to keep those World Series tickets while also being able to retain their Timeless Ticket to redeem for another game in any future season.

"We regret our mistake and look forward to welcoming them to American Family Field for their World Series experience," Schlesinger said.

stories.headline: Penguins' Ben Kindel hospitalized after medical emergency on flight
stories.summary: Penguins forward Ben Kindel was being evaluated at a Salt Lake City hospital Tuesday after having a medical emergency on the team's flight home from a four-game trip.
stories.body:
SALT LAKE CITY, Utah -- Pittsburgh Penguins forward Ben Kindel was being evaluated at a Salt Lake City hospital Tuesday after having a medical emergency on the team's flight home from a four-game trip.

The club said the 19-year-old Kindel had an unspecified issue shortly after the team's plane took off from the Salt Lake City airport on Tuesday.

The plane returned to the airport while Kindel was tended to on the flight by the team's medical staff. He was taken by ambulance to the University of Utah hospital.

The team said Kindel was conscious, alert and stable.

Kindel, in his second season with the Penguins after being selected with the No. 11 pick in the 2025 draft, has two goals and two assists in nine games. He played 18 minutes, 53 seconds in a 5-4 loss to Utah on Monday night.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem adamant F1 season will finish in Middle East despite ongoing conflict
stories.summary: Formula 1's season can and will finish in the Middle East as things stand, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has adamantly declared.
stories.body:
Formula 1's season can and will finish in the Middle East as things stand, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has adamantly declared.

F1 has races scheduled in Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6, but both are under a cloud of uncertainty and confusion due to ongoing tensions and hostilities in the Middle East.

F1 had promised its teams clarity by mid-October but that deadline has come and gone.

Sources from multiple teams have told ESPN they are still in the dark about whether F1 will go to those events or cancel and go to Italian circuit Imola, which is on stand-by to host a standalone finale on Dec. 6 if needed.

Ben Sulayem, head of motor racing's governing body, said the perceived danger of finishing the season as scheduled have been overblown and insisted it will be business as usual as things stand.

Asked if F1 was fine to finish the season as scheduled, Ben Sulayem is quoted as replying by The-Race: "Yeah - fine".

Ben Sulayem was speaking at an event in the UK, the opening of the FIA's new Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill on the outskirts of London.

He said he would not have gone there and left his family in the Middle East if he was worried about their safety.

"One thing I would say: I have my children there [in the UAE]. You think I would leave them there and I'm here now with you?

"You have to be sensible in this. Saying, 'Are we going to have an issue?' is one thing.

"But what you read in the media is actually different than what we have there. What we read and see on TV, we say, 'Where is it?' We don't have that, really. Otherwise why would I stay there? Why would I leave my family there?

"Does this say that there is nothing that is going to happen? I can't predict this.

"I can only tell you today that there is nothing and the two races are going to happen."

Runaway points leader Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of the title, but an escalation in hostilities in the Middle East and a cancellation before he has secured the title risks him being crowned champion via a press release because there would be one less event left in terms of points.

F1 has stuck to a similar line to the FIA president over recent weeks.

Speaking ahead of the rearranged Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, which was another event initially cancelled due to the Iran war, F1 boss Stefano Domenicali appeared to say the races were definitely going ahead.

"Yes, as we've already said, the calendar is confirmed: the last two Grands Prix will be in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. This is the direction we've taken based on the information and reassurances we have -- and which we absolutely must have, of course. It's the strategy we'll apply until the end of the year."

F1 later clarified Domenicali's use of the word "confirmed", insisting the final races are still subject to change if required. It is unclear whether any teams will have logistical issues taking staff to the Middle East as things stand.

- Lewis Hamilton 'hopes' F1 will race in the Middle East despite ongoing conflict

- Max Verstappen says he prefers F1 not to race in Middle East

- F1 still planning Middle East finale amid Kimi Antonelli title uncertainty - sources
Ben Sulayem claimed there would be no issue on the FIA side.

Asked if he would have any issue taking FIA staff to the Middle East, he replied: "I am happy, yes of course. Listen, I don't think the FIA staff would be more important to me than myself or my family. But if I am there it means I feel secure about this."

F1 was forced to cancel Bahrain and Saudi Arabia's events in April due to the war in Iran.

Re-arranging the Bahrain event in Malaysia meant F1 will only need a single race - Imola - to replace the final two and fulfil its contractual obligation to teams and broadcasters of hosting the minimum of 22 races.

stories.headline: A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?
stories.summary: The Ballon d'Or awards are typically tough to predict, but can ESPN and our global resources do just that?
stories.body:
The destination of the Ballon d'Or is typically tough to predict. Just ask Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who, in 2024, had spent weeks believing he would win the men's award only to learn hours ahead of the ceremony that it had gone to Manchester City midfielder Rodri instead.

This year, it is no less straightforward.

On the men's side, there are plenty of candidates: Teenager Lamine Yamal dazzled for Barcelona, Harry Kane scored more goals for Bayern Munich than he ever has before, Kylian Mbappé starred for Real Madrid, while the 2026 World Cup saw Lionel Messi and Rodri compete to be named the competition's best player (in the end, it went to Rodri).

And for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Alexia Putellas is the favorite after captaining Barcelona to another quadruple, but she was far from the only world-class player on that team.

The winners for both will be revealed on Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London, alongside a number of other awards, but is there a way to gauge who will walk away with the prizes ahead of time?

The men's Ballon d'Or is decided by a group of 100 journalists, each from different countries, while the Ballon d'Or Feminin's voting roll is made up of 50 journalists from 50 different countries. We decided to replicate that voting with ESPN journalists stationed all over the world.

Here's how we did it:

Methodology:

ESPN has a global team of journalists in every corner of the globe. We asked 20 ESPN journalists from around the world -- one per country -- to submit a ballot.
We used the official Ballon d'Or shortlists.
We had each voter submit their top five for the Ballon d'Or and their top three for all other awards.
Like official awards, each first-place vote received 15 points, followed by 12 points for second, 10 points for third, eight points for fourth and six points for fifth.

So, in a global experiment, can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or?

Jump to:

Ballon d'Or | Women's Ballon d'Or

Other awards

BALLON D'OR: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona, RW

What our voters said:

Josué Utrilla, ESPN Guatemala reporter: "I believe that being a world champion -- while playing a key role in Spain's attack and enjoying excellent form with Barcelona in LaLiga -- demonstrates the talent he possesses at such a young age (19) and has earned him a place among football's biggest stars."

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich, ST

What our voters said:
Tom Hamilton, ESPN UK senior writer: "Okay, he didn't win the World Cup, or the Champions League, but Kane's year is unsurpassed. He scored 73 goals in 65 matches across the England national team and Bayern. It's a freakish record, the like of which we'll never see again. Let's park sentimentality and aesthetic-influenced bias; this award rewards individual brilliance."

Thijs Zwagerman, ESPN NL reporter: "Despite scoring goals at an extraordinary rate for years, Kane still does not receive the full recognition he deserves on the international stage. His qualities extend far beyond his remarkable goal-scoring record. He possesses the rare ability for a striker to drop deep, influence the game from a deeper position and operate like a playmaker as well. While Kane has yet to win the Champions League or the World Cup, that does not diminish his individual brilliance. In my view, he was still the best player in the world on an individual level."

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami CF, FW

What our voters said:
Anirudh Menon, ESPN India editor: "If this award is to be given to the best footballer on the planet, there can only be one answer. He may be 39 years old; he may even be playing in Major League Soccer (where he did win the MLS Cup and topped almost every attacking chart in the league), but the 2026 World Cup showed just how vast the gulf between Messi and everyone else remains. When he turns it on, there isn't anyone close. Give him his ninth Ballon d'Or already."

Teo Coquet, ESPN Argentina reporter: "I choose him because of his attacking influence and ability to remain decisive on the international stage. His performance for Argentina at the World Cup is also a key factor in my evaluation. At 39 years old, he has played one of the best World Cups of his career."

Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid, ST

What our voters said:

Omar Flores, ESPN Mexico reporter: "Mbappé was the leading scorer across every competition he played in during the 2025-26 season, topping the charts in both the UEFA Champions League and Spain's LaLiga. At the World Cup, the France star scored 10 goals and became the tournament's all-time leading scorer (22 goals). Although he was unable to help his team advance beyond the semifinals, he remains one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d'Or. "

Carlos Valdez, ESPN Colombia reporter: "I would put Mbappé first because of his extraordinary ability to make the difference at the highest level. His pace, finishing, consistency and capacity to deliver in decisive moments make him one of the most influential players in world football. His goal-scoring achievements across the league, Champions League and World Cup further strengthen his case. For me, the Ballon d'Or should recognize not only outstanding numbers, but also a player's ability to change the course of a game, and Mbappé embodies that quality."

Fabián Ruiz, Paris Saint-Germain, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain reporter: "If we forget about the cameras, the spotlights, the commercial interests, and all the pomp that increasingly accompanies the business of football, then Ruiz should win the Ballon d'Or. I have no doubt about it. Why? It's simple. He was an undisputed and fundamental player for PSG's repeated Champions League title success last season, and was equally fundamental for Luis de la Fuente's victorious Spain side at the 2026 World Cup when Pedri wasn't at his best in midfield. Ruiz won it all over the past 12 months and was a standout player. He lacks marketing appeal, which will work against him, but he would be a deserving winner."

Rodri, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Jean Beausejour, ESPN Chile analyst: "In a World Cup year, winning the tournament carries enormous weight. Rodri had a tremendous influence on Spain's performances on football's biggest stage. Spain's ability to dominate matches, control the tempo and impose their style of play against different opponents was largely down to Rodri's intelligence, positioning and exceptional ability to dictate the game. His influence went far beyond individual statistics, making him, in my opinion, the most deserving candidate for the Ballon d'Or."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: HARRY KANE

In a symbol of how divisive the men's Ballon d'Or race is, Kane received half of the first-place votes but only one of the other 10 voters put him second. Perhaps the biggest surprise was the large snubbing of Yamal, who received just a single No. 1 vote.

This was a two-horse race and, as ESPN writer Bill Connelly wrote earlier this month: "Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal."

There is a slice of history on offer for Kane, too: Kane would be just the fifth Englishman to cradle the golden trophy, alongside Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

BALLON D'OR FEMININE: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES
Alexia Putellas, London City Lionesses, AM

What our voters said:

Leonard Solms, ESPN Africa reporter: "In her final season at Barcelona, midfield maestro Putellas not only captained Barcelona to the Liga F, UEFA Women's Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España trophies -- but also scored 20 goals and assisted 14 in 43 games. Capable of filling multiple roles in the team, Putellas is the kind of player any manager would love to have 11 of, and her brilliance should not be taken for granted."

Marissa Lordanic, ESPN Australia editor: "Putellas was once again invaluable across multiple competitions. The epitome of a big-game player, she ensured Barcelona's trophy case continued to grow before she tested herself in a new league."

Ewa Pajor, Barcelona, ST

What our voters said:

Gustavo Hofman, ESPN Brasil reporter: "Pajor combined outstanding individual production with collective success and delivered when it mattered most. She recorded 34 goals and eight assists in 46 appearances for club and country, helping Barcelona win the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup. Her intelligent movement and clinical finishing gave Barcelona a cutting edge throughout the season, but her Champions League performances ultimately put her ahead of the competition: she finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals and scored twice in the 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes in the final."

Ed Dove, ESPN Africa reporter: "In recent years, Pajor's performances haven't always been rewarded with the silverware and honors one might expect. That changed last term, where she was a key influence -- and a major goal threat -- in Barcelona's historic Quadruple-winning campaign. A genuine big-game player, she scored 33 across all competitions, including 11 in the Champions League, where she struck in every knockout round Barca played in before netting twice in a one-sided final victory over OL Lyonnes. Pajor may have scored fewer than she did during his remarkable debut season at Barca, but after overcoming the UWCL final defeat by Arsenal in 2025, she deserves the individual recognition here."

Temwa Chawinga, Kansas City Current, FW

What our voters said:

Jeff Kassouf, ESPN (US) reporter: "No player changes a game like Chawinga. She can create chances on her own in one-vs.-one situations from literally inside her own half on the counter attack, and is a sharp goal scorer. Scoring 20 goals in the NWSL and then following that up with 15 the next season is dominant form at a world-class level. And she does it for club and country, having helped lowly Malawi to the 2027 World Cup. This time next year, more international opponents will know the fear of having Chawinga run at their defense."

Patri Guijarro, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain: "The backbone of Barcelona's women's team and an excellent midfielder who makes runs from the second line. Other players usually steal the spotlight, but her talent is unquestionable. She makes the rest of the team shine."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: ALEXIA PUTELLAS
This result is not a surprise. Putellas is the clear favourite for the award, and our voters agreed.

Putellas enjoyed a dream end to her 14-year Barcelona career last season, captaining the club to a second Quadruple in three years, including lifting the Women's Champions League, before she moved to captain London City Lionesses, who are now third in the Women's Super League after five games.

stories.body:
The NBA is back with a bang.

The 2026-27 season tips off with a tripleheader, beginning with a rare daytime game between the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics. That sets up ring night at Madison Square Garden as the New York Knicks host the Philadelphia 76ers. The night concludes with a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference finals between the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder.

Each game bring its own headlines, starting off in Detroit. The Pistons defeated the Celtics 121-113 after a big fourth quarter from Duncan Robinson who helped Detroit go on a 23-0 run, after being down 22 points. It marks the franchise's largest come-from-behind win over the Celtics over the last 30 seasons, according to ESPN Research.

The Knicks are raising a banner for the first time in 50 years. Who will look to spoil their night? None other than the new-look 76ers, with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James teaming up with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

Five months after defeating Oklahoma City in Game 7 to reach the Finals, San Antonio welcomes its Western Conference rivals in another battle. The Thunder and Spurs return most of their cores, setting up a matchup full of familiar matchups and tension.

We'll have all of the top moments and highlights from the NBA's tripleheader. Follow along below.

stories.headline: Commanders' Quinn, Daniels discuss QB's throwaway on fourth-down play
stories.summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's loss, coach Dan Quinn said.
stories.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn said.

On a fourth-and-2 from the 49ers' 13-yard line, Daniels dropped back to pass and left the pocket after the 49ers started to generate pressure.

As Daniels ran to his right, two defenders pursued him, including linebacker Fred Warner. A flag was also thrown in front of Daniels. He could not make the first down running and with no open receiver in front of him he threw the ball away.

Quinn said he spoke to Daniels about the play.

"Even when you know there's a penalty, you still take your shot, man, to go throw it, complete it," Quinn said. "You don't know if it's gonna get picked up."

As it turned out the penalty wasn't an offside call on the defense, which would have given Washington a first down. Rather it was an illegal shift on the Commanders.

"I didn't know. It could have been offside, it could have been on us," Daniels said on whether he anticipated an offside call.

San Francisco declined the penalty because of the incompletion.

The throwaway came one week after Daniels failed to throw a pass away with eight seconds left in overtime to stop the clock. Instead, he was tackled and the clock expired, preventing a chance to attempt a game-winning 42-yard field goal.

Offensive coordinator David Blough and Quinn both blamed themselves for the play call and failure to simply call for a spike.

Daniels did complete 29 of 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. He helped Washington rally from a 20-3 halftime deficit and drove the Commanders deep into 49ers territory late in the game with a chance to take the lead.

"Like most things with him, there's some plays that you said, that's an incredible throw," Quinn said. "And there's other ones I'd love him to stay through the [read]."

He said he knew it would be tough for Daniels to gain yards scrambling because of the 49ers' team speed and their zone coverage with eyes on the quarterback. Indeed he rushed only four times for 10 yards.

Daniels was playing his second game wearing a brace on his left elbow that he dislocated in Week 2. Quinn said as Daniels evolves in Blough's offense he'd like him to scramble more to throw. But he also knows he can make plays multiple ways.

"He always can make some throws that just kinda leaves you thinking, 'Man, there it is. There's only a few guys that can make that throw or that play,'" Quinn said.

stories.headline: Ngumoha sparks Liverpool's comeback Champions League win
stories.summary: Still just 18, Rio Ngumoha produced the finest game of his Liverpool career thus far in helping the Reds overturn a two-goal deficit vs. Villarreal.
stories.body:
LIVERPOOL, England -- Rio Ngumoha's reputation must have preceded him. Liverpool's UEFA Champions League clash with Villarreal was only a few minutes old, and already the opposition defenders had begun to double-team the young forward in an attempt to stop him wreaking havoc down the right flank.

Their efforts proved futile; Ngumoha provided two outstanding assists to help Liverpool come from 2-0 down to claim a 4-3 victory at Anfield. The England international did not manage to get on the scoresheet, but he produced what was undeniably the most accomplished display of his fledgling senior career, providing Andoni Iraola's side with the impetus required to overcome its sluggish start and secure a third straight win in all competitions.

"It's up there with one of the best I've played," Ngumoha told Amazon Prime postmatch. "I enjoyed myself and the team helped me a lot. Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one v. one or two v. one, I believe in myself. I'll just keep going and be ruthless."

Ngumoha came into this season with a point to prove. Having broken into Liverpool's first team as a left winger under Arne Slot last term, the forward has found his route to regular game time in his favored position stymied by the summer arrival of the £123 million Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

The further addition of Víctor Muñoz from Osasuna, plus the renaissance of Cody Gakpo, has only served to intensify competition in attack. It is the kind of challenge that some young players might have shied away from, but on the evidence of his most recent display, it has spurred Ngumoha on to new heights.

"Any position -- right wing, left wing -- I just try my best especially on the ball just to beat my man as best as I can," Ngumoha told ESPN during preseason. "The more I keep learning in training and games, I'll definitely improve. To be adaptable is a skill that I need, definitely."

That versatility has paid dividends for Ngumoha over the past few weeks. The 18-year-old started on the right against LASK Linz last week before impressing in the same position in his cameo against Brentford at the weekend.

Tuesday night, though, was a coming of age. Ngumoha became the youngest player on record (since 2008-09) to complete five-plus dribbles (7), have 10-plus touches in the opposition box (12) and register an assist (2) in a Champions League match.

His relentlessness and ability to torment defenders showed that, while Liverpool might not have signed a like-for-like replacement for the talismanic Mohamed Salah, they still have a potent attacking threat on the right-hand side.

Certainly, Ngumoha's flair and dynamism was needed against Villarreal given how poorly Liverpool had started the game. The Reds found themselves a goal down inside four minutes after a lapse from Virgil van Dijk opened the door for Villarreal's Georges Mikautadze to slot home past Alisson.

Things went from bad to worse for the hosts shortly before the half-hour mark when Sergi Cardona was given the freedom of the Liverpool penalty area to coolly double Villarreal's lead. It was a rare moment of joy for the left back on an evening when Ngumoha's exploits regularly had him in retreat.

A fine Alexis Mac Allister header from a Kostas Tsimikas corner halved the deficit for Liverpool before the break, but it was Ngumoha who really sparked the game into life, seeing off the attentions of three defenders to curl a fabulous cross toward the far post for Ronald Araújo to nod home.

The 18-year-old's assist for Mac Allister in the second half was even more impressive as he drove inside from the right and flashed a sumptuous ball across the face of goal. From there, the impressive Mac Allister was only too happy to oblige. The icing on the cake was provided by substitute Florian Wirtz, who netted his first Liverpool goal since April after a cutback from Gakpo.

Villarreal made it nervy when Tani Oluwaseyi finished at the far post three minutes from time. But the Reds managed to hang on, marking the first time they have come from two goals down to win a game in any competition since May 2022, when they beat Villarreal 3-2 to book their spot in the Champions League final.

By the time Oluwaseyi scored, Ngumoha was watching the action from the bench, having been substituted to a well-deserved standing ovation.

"I am happy with his attitude," Iraola said of the forward in his postmatch news conference. "He is eager to improve the things we think he needs to improve. He is eager to add more things to his game. He has changed sides a lot. He has played a lot on the right lately.

"He is feeling so comfortable now. He is adding some shots from the left. He hasn't scored, but he is getting there, and if he can add these small things to his game, it will put him in a better position.

That's the good thing with Rio. He is only 18, he's still not the full package. He can add things, fortunately for us also. I hope he can continue the same way. It is not always going to be like this -- there will be ups and downs in the process -- but I'm happy because he is in a great place."

While Iraola has plenty of decisions to make ahead of Liverpool's meeting with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday, the inclusion of Ngumoha in his starting lineup must surely now be viewed as a foregone conclusion. The teenager hasn't started a Premier League game since Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Newcastle United on the opening weekend, but he could hardly have delivered a more compelling audition than his display against Villarreal.

As the Liverpool players made their way toward the Kop to applaud at the full-time whistle, Duran Duran's "Rio" blasted out from the Anfield speakers. If Ngumoha continues on his current trajectory, it is surely destined to become a regular serenade.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey warning signs: D-men with hot starts to consider trading away
stories.summary: Sean dives into the defensemen trends to find warning signs for hot starters and what managers should do.
stories.body:
Last week, we looked at how little the early goalie standings tell you. Skaters aren't much easier to predict, but power-play time offers a useful clue. Especially for defensemen.

How many of the top 25 (by position) at this point of the season were still top-25 at the end:

2025-26: 10 forwards, nine defenders, 10 goalies

2024-25: 11 forwards, 11 defenders, 15 goalies

2023-24: 13 forwards, 16 defenders, 15 goalies

2022-23: 14 forwards, 12 defenders, 16 goalies

2021-22: 10 forwards, 10 defenders, 17 goalies

2020-21: 11 forwards, 13 defenders, 13 goalies

What the players who maintained their value averaged, compared with the ones who fell out (six-season averages):

Forwards who stayed: 4:00 PP TOI/GP, 0.59 blocks and 1.05 hits per game

Forwards who fell out: 3:21 PP TOI/GP, 0.61 blocks and 1.01 hits per game

Defenders who stayed: 2:48 PP TOI/GP, 2.06 blocks and 1.33 hits per game

Defenders who fell out: 1:58 PP TOI/GP, 2.05 blocks and 1.30 hits per game

Hits and blocks didn't separate them. Power-play time did, especially on the blue line. That puts these early leaders among defenders on watch:

MacKenzie Weegar, D, Utah Mammoth (available in 2.1% of ESPN leagues): fourth among defenders, 0:10 PP TOI/GP

Vladislav Gavrikov, D, New York Rangers (available in 32.3%): sixth among defenders, 0:04 PP TOI/GP

Travis Sanheim, D, Philadelphia Flyers (available in 30.8%): 10th among defenders, 0:14 PP TOI/GP

Declan Carlile, D, Pittsburgh Penguins (available in 57.5%): 12th among defenders, no PP time

Nick Seeler, D, Philadelphia Flyers (available in 84.6%): 16th among defenders, no PP time

Tyler Kleven, D, Ottawa Senators (available in 76.9%): 20th among defenders, 0:03 PP TOI/GP

Two weeks ago, this column called Gavrikov the easiest add of the early hits-and-blocks crowd. He has been worth it so far, but history says that kind of start rarely lasts without power-play time. Enjoy the blocks while they're paying off, just don't count on him staying sixth.

Among forwards, the stars clear the bar on talent alone. Connor McDavid averages 3:16 on the power play, and nobody is trading him. The ones to worry about are the passengers. Vasily Podkolzin ranks 11th among forwards, largely by riding with McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, and he gets 3:07 on the power play after finishing 107th last season. Artturi Lehkonen is 24th with just 1:48. If someone in your league is valuing their starts, this is the time to trade them away.

Hill is 4-0-0 with good starts (2.4 fantasy points or more) in three of four and ranks 10th in FPP60 (fantasy points per 60 minutes), and he and Hart have strictly alternated over the past four games. Nedeljkovic took two of three starts last week and ranks 12th in FPP60, while Askarov ranks 52nd and hasn't delivered a good start in his past three. The Sharks play five times in the next 10 days, and Nedeljkovic is available in 95% of leagues.

Last week, Tarasov was a speculative add. Two good starts in two tries later, he leads all goalies in FPP60, and the Red Wings have strictly alternated over the past four games. Calgary (30th in scoring) and Chicago (29th) are both on the schedule over the next 10 days.

Daccord's soft schedule didn't save him. He lost 10.2 fantasy points last week, and Grubauer took two of three starts. Grubauer now has the better save percentage (.909 to .882) and FPP60 rank (24th to 35th), and with all four of Seattle's next games at home, he's the better bet in a true timeshare.

Edmonton Oilers in eight games (three last week):

Levi is 4-1-0 with good starts in three of five, and his rostership has more than doubled in a week, yet he's still available in 68% of leagues. The Oilers' next five games are all at home, including Detroit (27th in scoring) and Calgary (30th), though Jarry has taken two of the past four starts.

Follow-ups from last week:

Dylan Garand, G, New York Rangers (available in 41.5%): Five straight starts and good starts in five of six overall. The Rangers play only three times in the next 10 days, but he shouldn't be on any waiver wire.

Ivar Stenberg, LW, San Jose Sharks (available in 61.0%): Stenberg already has five power-play points, and the top unit he shares with Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith, Alex Wennberg and Dmitry Orlov has scored four goals in 13:51 together while generating 4.19 shot attempts per two minutes. He's logging 5:36 a night on the advantage.

Neal Pionk, D, Winnipeg Jets (available in 64.5%): Pionk has quarterbacked the Jets' top unit in all three of their past games, taking 71% of the team's power-play time, and his 2.12 FPPG is the best of any defender on this list. He has almost two weeks of runway left while Josh Morrissey is sidelined with a wrist injury.

Chandler Stephenson, C, Seattle Kraken (available in 91.6%): Two weeks ago, we doubted the Kraken's kids would keep the top unit. They didn't: Stephenson, Jordan Eberle, Jared McCann, Bobby McMann and Vince Dunn are back on it, and the group has scored four times in 16:30. Stephenson has two power-play points in his past three games.

Morgan Frost, C, Calgary Flames (available in 94.3%): The Flames' original top unit is back together after a brief swap, and Frost has two power-play points in his past three games with a 1.84 FPPG. Calgary plays twice this week and four times next week.

Ryan Leonard, RW, Washington Capitals (available in 65.9%): Leonard has held a top-unit spot alongside Alex Ovechkin for three straight games, playing 57 percent of the Capitals' power-play time, and he's at 1.91 FPPG.

Follow-ups from earlier columns:

Maxim Shabanov, RW, Minnesota Wild (available in 93.3%): Still on a top unit that has scored five times in 28:34, and the Wild play four games this week.

Brayden Schenn, C/LW, New York Islanders (available in 77.2%): The Islanders' top unit has cooled since Simon Holmstrom replaced Matias Maccelli, and Schenn has no power-play points in his past three games. Hold off.

Kasperi Kapanen, RW, Edmonton Oilers (available in 94.8%): Zach Hyman is back on the top unit, and Kapanen is off it. That was quick.

Kent Johnson, LW/RW, Columbus Blue Jackets (available in 84.6%): Columbus has restored its original top unit, and Johnson is at 1.80 FPPG.

Dmitry Orlov, D, San Jose Sharks (available in 88.1%): Orlov has taken over Luca Cagnoni's quarterback spot on the Sharks' top unit.

Droppables

Same caution as last week: this list flags rostered players whose production has lagged, and it still catches plenty of stars. Sidney Crosby (1.4 FPPG), Wyatt Johnston (1.4), Dylan Larkin (1.5), Artemi Panarin (1.7), Adrian Kempe (1.7), Mark Scheifele (1.7), Brayden Point (1.3) and Lucas Raymond (1.2) all qualify. All of them are on their team's top power-play unit, and none of them is going anywhere.

But as this week's intro showed, power-play time is what separates the players who hold their value from the ones who fade. These three have lost it:

Noah Dobson, D, Montreal Canadiens (rostered in 93.5%): Dobson is logging 21:33 a night but isn't on either power-play unit, because Lane Hutson runs both. That's a problem for a defender whose fantasy value has always leaned on the man advantage, and at 1.3 FPPG he's the clearest drop candidate on this list in standard leagues.

Dylan Cozens, C/RW, Ottawa Senators (rostered in 76.1%): Claude Giroux took Cozens' spot on the top power-play unit Friday, and Cozens was already at just 1.1 FPPG. He's movable in shallow leagues.

Morgan Rielly, D, Toronto Maple Leafs (rostered in 78.2%): Darren Raddysh has the top-unit quarterback job, and Rielly has been relegated to the second unit. At 1.2 FPPG, there are better defenders on most waiver wires, including a couple in this week's power-play section.

On notice:

Vincent Trocheck, C, Utah Mammoth (rostered in 87.6%): 16:18 a night, second power-play unit, 1.3 FPPG.

Alex Ovechkin, LW/RW, Washington Capitals (rostered in 88.9%): Still on the top power-play unit, but his 13:56 a night is the lowest ice time on this list, and he's at 1.0 FPPG.

Follow-ups from last week:

Sam Bennett has climbed from 1.05 FPPG to 1.6. Keep him.

John Tavares could be stashed, but if you're facing tough decisions with limited IR space, you can also let him go. He's expected out until almost December.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: Christian Horner opposed Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull move: 'Shouldn't have been promoted'
stories.summary: Christian Horner has opened up on his reservations about Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull tenure in 2025, claiming the New Zealander "really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."
stories.body:
Christian Horner has opened up on his reservations about Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull tenure in 2025, claiming the New Zealander "really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

The inexperienced Lawson was surprisingly picked to replace Sergio Pérez as Max Verstappen's new teammate in December 2024, but former team boss Horner says in his new autobiography, Drive, that he was uneasy with the decision and that it was Red Bull adviser Helmut Marko who pushed for the promotion.

Lawson was dropped after only two races, before Red Bull swiftly turned to Yuki Tsunoda.

"Liam was another racer from the junior programme and Helmut had championed the promotion, but I felt uncomfortable," Horner wrote.

"He was young and inexperienced, with only eleven Formula One races to his name, and we would be asking a huge amount from him."

Horner also accused Marko of playing political games over the decision, claiming the Austrian had told Lawson he was responsible for securing the drive.

"Meanwhile, Helmut was playing games," Horner wrote. "Before the final race of the season in Abu Dhabi, he had informed Liam that he would be driving for Red Bull because of his influence.

"When I challenged Helmut on this, he typically denied everything."

Lawson was promoted following Pérez's difficult 2024 campaign, which saw Red Bull finish third in the constructors' championship despite Verstappen winning his fourth consecutive drivers' title.

The New Zealander had impressed during two spells with the team's junior outfit but struggled immediately after stepping up to Red Bull.

He qualified 18th for the season-opening Australian Grand Prix before crashing out of the race, and then qualified last for both the sprint and the race in China.

"Liam only lasted two races," Horner wrote. "He struggled in pre-season testing and was clearly uncomfortable with the RB21's difficult handling characteristics.

"His confidence was smashed and, as with Pierre Gasly and Alex Albon, his arrival at Red Bull had come too soon.

"Sensing that the pressure on Liam was unfair, we replaced him."

- Horner: Red Bull blocked moves for Leclerc and Alonso

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How he could shake up Ferrari's future

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title at the US Grand Prix

Horner said Honda, Red Bull's engine partner at the time, welcomed the decision to promote Japanese driver Tsunoda.

"The move back [to Racing] Bulls was tough for Liam," Horner wrote. "But he really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

Lawson returned to Racing Bulls, while Tsunoda remained alongside Verstappen for the rest of the 2025 season.

Horner was subsequently dismissed as Red Bull team principal and CEO in July 2025.

Lawson said earlier this year that Red Bull created a false narrative around the reasons behind his early exit from the team. The 24-year-old said he wasn't "mentally struggling" and that Red Bull had actually pushed him towards a "wild" setup change to find performance, which ultimately hampered his pace. He added that he now pretends in his mind he "never even went there."

Drive, Christian Horner's autobiography, will be released on Oct. 22.

stories.headline: Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili joins rare list of trilogy bouts at UFC 333
stories.summary: ESPN categorizes all 19 of the UFC's trilogies ahead of Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili 3 at UFC 333 on Saturday.
stories.body:
When men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan and former champion Merab Dvalishvili fight in the UFC 333 co-main event on Saturday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, it will be their third meeting, completing the promotion's 20th trilogy.

This weekend's headliners, featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski and undefeated challenger Movsar Evloev, will square off for the first time, but Volkanovski has already been part of a UFC trilogy. His threepeat with Max Holloway several years ago played out far differently from what will unfold in the UFC 333 co-main. That's guaranteed. (Read on to find out why.)

How fitting is it that Saturday's event is numbered 333, a coincidental acknowledgment that when the UFC deals out three of a kind, the fans end up with a winning hand. Usually.

Trilogies come in all shapes with all sizes. Many of the sport's biggest stars have been in one or more, yet at least one UFC three-fight series featured competitors newer fans probably haven't heard of. Some trilogies have had championship-level stakes in each fight, while others have been driven by nothing but a scornful rivalry that makes the fights feel no less consequential. A few trilogies have been one-sided and a couple have concluded without establishing who's better. We did the math.

Other MMA organizations have staged trilogies, and some have played out across multiple promotions, but this list sticks to the 19 all-UFC trilogies to date and sorts them by similarities and distinguishing factors.

Passing the torch
Trilogies in which the winner of the first fight was at the top of the sport, and by the third meeting the opponent was MMA's top fighter

Chuck Liddell vs. Randy Couture
Results:

UFC 43, June 6, 2003: Couture def. Liddell (TKO3) for interim light heavyweight title
UFC 52, April 16, 2005: Liddell def. Couture (KO1) for light heavyweight title
UFC 57, Feb. 4, 2006: Liddell def. Couture (KO2) for light heavyweight title

Notable: In the lead-up to their second meeting, Liddell and Couture coached against each other on the inaugural season of "The Ultimate Fighter," the reality show UFC CEO Dana White often credits with keeping the UFC in business. Through their TV appearances and contrasting fighting styles and personalities, Liddell and Couture helped catapult MMA toward the sports mainstream. Couture is one of just three fighters (along with Tito Ortiz and Matt Hughes) to compete in two UFC trilogies -- this one and a trio of fights with Vitor Belfort.

Georges St-Pierre vs. Matt Hughes
Results:

UFC 50, Oct. 22, 2004: Hughes def. St-Pierre (Sub1) for welterweight title
UFC 65, Nov. 18, 2006: St-Pierre def. Hughes (TKO2) for welterweight title
UFC 79, Dec. 29, 2007: St-Pierre def. Hughes (Sub2) for interim welterweight title

Notable: This is the only UFC trilogy to feature multiple submission finishes. Hughes won by armbar at UFC 50, and St-Pierre ended the trilogy at UFC 79 by submitting Hughes, also by armbar. When the fighters were standing, though, GSP dominated. In their second meeting, he outstruck Hughes 49-10 with two knockdowns. In the third fight, it was 97-10.

A stunning start ... and finish
Trilogies that began with a shocking KO upset, followed by the KO victim scoring two dominant wins

Cain Velasquez vs. Junior Dos Santos
Results:

UFC on Fox, Nov. 12, 2011: Dos Santos def. Velasquez (KO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 155, Dec. 29, 2012: Velasquez def. Dos Santos (UD) for heavyweight title
UFC 166, Oct. 19, 2013: Velasquez def. Dos Santos (TKO5) for heavyweight title

Notable: The first fight lasted barely a minute, as Dos Santos essentially won by one-punch knockout. The rematch and trilogy fight dramatically swung the other way. Velasquez battered JDS for the full 25 minutes of their second meeting, as reflected by one judge awarding him two 10-8 rounds. Velasquez became the first UFC fighter to reach triple-figure significant strikes (111) and double-figure takedowns (11) in a single fight.

Stipe Miocic vs. Daniel Cormier
Results:

UFC 226, July 7, 2018: Cormier def. Miocic (KO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 241, Aug. 17, 2019: Miocic def. Cormier (TKO4) for heavyweight title
UFC 252, Aug. 15, 2020: Miocic def. Cormier (UD) for heavyweight title

Notable: Cormier was light heavyweight champion when he first faced Miocic, and by crushing the heavyweight king with an uppercut, Cormier became the second UFC champ to reign in two weight classes simultaneously. Miocic bounced back in the next two fights, and his victory in the third meeting tied him with Couture for the most UFC heavyweight title-fight wins, with six.

Back and forth (and back)
Trilogies in which the winner of the first fight lost the second, then won the third -- a rarity

Randy Couture vs. Vitor Belfort
Results:

UFC 15, Oct. 17, 1997: Couture def. Belfort (TKO1)
UFC 46, Jan. 31, 2004: Belfort def. Couture (TKO1) for light heavyweight title
UFC 49, Aug. 21, 2004: Couture def. Belfort (TKO3) for light heavyweight title

Notable: Entering the first fight, Belfort was 20 years old and 4-0 as a pro -- all knockouts of a minute, 17 seconds or faster. But Couture, 34, stopped his momentum cold. When they met again six years later, Belfort won in 49 seconds after his glove scraped Couture's eye, causing a corneal abrasion that prompted the cageside doctor to stop the fight. In the third fight, Couture brutalized Belfort for three rounds before that event's doctor had seen enough. This is the only UFC trilogy in which two fights ended by doctor's stoppage.

BJ Penn vs. Matt Hughes
Results:

UFC 46, Jan. 31, 2004: Penn def. Hughes (Sub1) for welterweight title
UFC 63, Sept. 23, 2006: Hughes def. Penn (TKO3) for welterweight title
UFC 123, Nov. 20, 2010: Penn def. Hughes (KO1)

Notable: After two unsuccessful bids for the lightweight championship, Penn moved up to welterweight and won the belt in a stunning upset, ending Hughes' two-year reign and 13-fight winning streak. After Hughes won the rematch to even the score, Penn completed the trilogy in style, knocking out Hughes in 21 seconds -- the fastest finish in a UFC trilogy.

You're just flexing now
Trilogies that ended in a 3-0 sweep

Tito Ortiz vs. Ken Shamrock
Results:

UFC 40, Nov. 12, 2002: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO3) for light heavyweight title
UFC 61, July 8, 2006: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO1)
UFC Ortiz vs. Shamrock 3, Oct. 10, 2006: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO1)

Notable: This trilogy is unmatched in its bitter animosity, for sure, and maybe even in one-sidedness. The feud grew out of the brash Ortiz defeating fighters from Shamrock's highly regarded Lion's Den gym, then mocking that team with vulgar gestures and custom T-shirts. Ortiz and Shamrock finally met at UFC 40 amid much anticipation, and the heated buildup drove a pay-per-view buy rate double what the UFC had ever seen.

Frankie Edgar vs. BJ Penn
Results:

UFC 112, April 10, 2010: Edgar def. Penn (UD) for lightweight title
UFC 118, Aug. 28, 2010: Edgar def. Penn (UD) for lightweight title
The Ultimate Fighter 19 Finale, July 6, 2014: Edgar def. Penn (TKO3)

Notable: Penn, who had not lost a lightweight bout in eight years, was a near 8-1 betting favorite in the first fight. Even after Edgar pulled off a narrow upset, he was still the underdog entering the rematch. He won that one more clearly with three 50-45 scorecards, then completed the trilogy with a knockout. Of the UFC's 19 trilogies, 11 have ended with a finish in the third fight. But only two -- both involving Edgar -- ended with a finish after two consecutive decisions. The other was Edgar's series with Gray Maynard.

Alexander Volkanovski vs. Max Holloway
Results:

UFC 245, Dec. 14, 2019: Volkanovski def. Holloway (UD) for featherweight title
UFC 251, July 11, 2020: Volkanovski def. Holloway (SD) for featherweight title
UFC 276, July 2, 2022: Volkanovski def. Holloway (UD) for featherweight title

Notable: Just because this trilogy ended 3-0 doesn't mean Volkanovski had it easy. In the second fight, Holloway knocked him down in each of the first two rounds, forcing the champ to play catch-up. Holloway made Volkanovski work the full five rounds in all three fights. At 75 minutes of total cage time, this is the UFC's longest trilogy.

Let's call it even
Trilogies that ended at 1-1, plus a draw

Frankie Edgar vs. Gray Maynard
Results:

UFC Fight Night, April 2, 2008: Maynard def. Edgar (UD)
UFC 125, Jan. 1, 2011: Maynard vs. Edgar for lightweight title ends in split draw
UFC 136, Oct. 8, 2011: Edgar def. Maynard (KO4) for lightweight title

Notable: The second meeting produced the greatest comeback and the most memorable draw in UFC history. Maynard knocked Edgar down three times in Round 1 while piling up a 47-10 edge in strikes landed. All three judges scored it 10-8, and Edgar was so rocked that he doesn't remember anything from the rounds that followed. He "missed" a great fight. The final meeting also began badly for Edgar, but this time his comeback built toward a late knockout that emphatically evened the score.

Valentina Shevchenko vs. Alexa Grasso
Results:

UFC 285, March 4, 2023: Grasso def. Shevchenko (Sub4) for women's flyweight title
Noche UFC, Sept. 16, 2023: Shevchenko vs. Grasso for women's flyweight title ends in split draw
UFC 306, Sept. 14, 2024: Shevchenko def. Grasso (UD) for women's flyweight title

Notable: The only women's trilogy in UFC history opened with a staggering upset, as Grasso capitalized on an ill-advised spinning attack by Shevchenko to seize control and quickly lock in a choke that ended the champ's six-year unbeaten run. Grasso narrowly held on to the title in a tightly contested second fight. Shevchenko dominated the third meeting, thanks to a change in strategy. Her grappling-heavy approach produced at least one takedown in each of the five rounds, 16 minutes of ground control and a trio of 50-45 scorecards.

Remember me?
Trilogies with at least seven years between fights

Dustin Poirier vs. Max Holloway
Results:

UFC 143, Feb. 4, 2012: Poirier def. Holloway (Sub1) for interim lightweight title
UFC 236, April 13, 2019: Poirier def. Holloway (UD)
UFC 318, July 19, 2025: Holloway def. Poirier (UD) for BMF title

Notable: The first fight was Holloway's UFC debut at 20 years old, and their final meeting 13 years later was Poirier's retirement fight. By winning that third bout, Holloway became the first fighter to win a UFC trilogy after losing the first two matchups.

Leon Edwards vs. Kamaru Usman
Results:

UFC on Fox, Dec. 19, 2015: Usman def. Edwards (UD)
UFC 278, Aug. 20, 2022: Edwards def. Usman (KO5) for welterweight title
UFC 268, March 18, 2023: Edwards def. Usman (MD) for welterweight title

Notable: Usman was 58 seconds from going up 2-0 in this series when an Edwards head kick out of nowhere changed everything. Usman had won 15 fights in a row and was on the verge of tying Anderson Silva's record for the longest UFC win streak at the time. Since that shocking defeat, he's gone 1-3, including another loss to Edwards.

No gold, just (a little) glory
Trilogies in which no championships were on the line

Sam Stout vs. Spencer Fisher
Results:

UFC 58, March 4, 2006: Stout def. Fisher (SD)
UFC Fight Night, June 12, 2007: Fisher def. Stout (UD)
UFC on FX, June 22, 2012: Stout def. Fisher (UD)

Notable: The first meeting was Stout's UFC debut, and apparently both fighters were just warming up. The rematch and trilogy fight each earned fight of the night bonuses. The third meeting had an added emotional element for Stout, as it was his first fight after the death of his coach and brother-in-law, Shawn Tompkins.

Forrest Griffin vs. Tito Ortiz
Results:

UFC 59, April 15, 2006: Ortiz def. Griffin (SD)
UFC 106, Nov. 21, 2009: Griffin def. Ortiz (SD)
UFC 148, July 7, 2012: Griffin def. Ortiz (UD)

Notable: Both competitors were 205-pound champions, just not during any of their three meetings. All three fights happened after Ortiz's title reign from 2000 to 2003. The first fight was before Griffin became champ in 2008, and the other two were after he lost the belt later that same year. The trilogy fight was Griffin's career finale and Ortiz's final UFC appearance.

Charles Oliveira vs. Nik Lentz
Results:

UFC on Versus, June 26, 2011: Oliveira vs. Lentz ends in no contest
UFC Fight Night, May 30, 2015: Oliveira def. Lentz (Sub3)
UFC Fight Night, May 18, 2019: Oliveira def. Lentz (TKO2)

Notable: The first bout appeared to end with an Oliveira rear-naked choke in Round 2, but the Pennsylvania State Athletic Commission ruled that Oliveira had landed an illegal knee and overturned the result to a no-contest. The bout earned both men fight of the night bonuses, as did the second fight.

Dustin Poirier vs. Conor McGregor
Results:

UFC 178, Sept. 27, 2014: McGregor def. Poirier (TKO1)
UFC 257, Jan. 23, 2021: Poirier def. McGregor (TKO2)
UFC 264, July 10, 2021: Poirier def. McGregor (TKO1)

Notable: This rivalry could have fit in the "Remember me?" category because of the seven-year gap between the first and second bouts. But what truly makes this trilogy stand apart from all others is McGregor's star power. He headlined the seven highest-selling pay-per-views in UFC history, and only his bouts with Khabib Nurmagomedov and Nate Diaz outsold his two meetings with Poirier in 2021. McGregor suffered the first two knockout losses of his MMA career in those bouts, the second finish coming by doctor's stoppage after he broke his left tibia and fibula.

Three is not enough?
The only UFC tetralogy -- plus 75% of another

Brandon Moreno vs. Deiveson Figueiredo
Results:

UFC 256, Dec. 12, 2020: Moreno vs. Figueiredo for men's flyweight title ends in majority draw
UFC 263, June 12, 2021: Moreno def. Figueiredo (Sub3) for men's flyweight title
UFC 270, Jan. 22, 2022: Figueiredo def. Moreno (UD) for men's flyweight title
UFC 283, Jan. 21, 2023: Moreno def. Figueiredo (TKO3) for men's flyweight title

Notable: These two flyweights squeezed in four fights over 25 months, faster than many two-fight series. Moreno and Figueiredo each produced heart-pounding moments throughout the four fights, and together they landed exactly 700 strikes. The second fight represented a memorable accomplishment for Moreno when he became the first Mexico-born UFC champion.

Tim Sylvia vs. Andrei Arlovski
Results:

UFC 51, Feb. 5, 2005: Arlovski def. Sylvia (Sub1) for interim heavyweight title
UFC 59, April 15, 2006: Sylvia def. Arlovski (TKO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 61, July 8, 2006: Sylvia def. Arlovski (UD) for heavyweight title
One FC 5, Aug. 31, 2012: Sylvia vs. Arlovski ends no contest in One Championship

Notable: The first fight lasted 47 seconds, with Arlovski's quick knockdown leading to a leg-lock finish. Arlovski nearly repeated the feat in the rematch, dropping Sylvia halfway through Round 1. But after a wobbly Sylvia got back to his feet and Arlovski moved in for a finish, Sylvia caught him with a short uppercut to even the score. Their final UFC meeting turned into a tactical, tentative sparring session, as one might expect from a matchup where each fighter had already felt the other's power. Also as expected, the ornery crowd was unimpressed.
